articles.title: Camo: M81 Woodland
articles.summary: Dark olive-green camo of soft organic blobs in four earthy tones, semi-matte, faintly sparkly. Reads as dark, busy military green camo; at distance the khaki flecks light it up a little and the black-green gives depth, but it never gets coarse.
articles.what: Four colours, organic blobs, and the pattern every army copied for thirty years. Up close: Small jagged blobs of near-black green, mid olive, drab green and khaki tan, packed densely with hard edges and no flat area bigger than a thumbnail. Blobs are 4-20px, with the tan mostly as little flecks. From a distance: Reads as dark, busy military green camo; at distance the khaki flecks light it up a little and the black-green gives depth, but it never gets coarse. Measured spec (average): metal 6, roughness 138, coat 121. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.

articles.title: Hardware: Parkerised
articles.summary: Flat dark grey phosphate metal, even satin sheen, faint fine grain, no colour at all. Reads as a flat dark neutral gunmetal grey with slight speckle; no colour tint, a plain stealth grey that can look like primer.
articles.what: Manganese phosphate, porous by design so it holds oil in the surface. Up close: Neutral dark grey with a fine pitted grain: scattered tiny dark pores with pale rims, 2-4 px, and faint lighter clouds. Colourless; looks like phosphate-coated steel or a bead-blasted gun part. From a distance: Reads as a flat dark neutral gunmetal grey with slight speckle; no colour tint, a plain stealth grey that can look like primer. Measured spec (average): metal 151, roughness 78, coat 59. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Hardware: Parkerised" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body as a quiet base
Hood, roof and sides: grain suits broad panels; bumpers and trim match
Dark neutral ground: white, orange or yellow numbers read clearly; grey or black numbers vanish.
Bold orange, white or olive stripes: tactical contrast that stops it reading as primer
Pairs well with: olive drab, black, orange, white.
pitfalls: Not gloss gunmetal paint: satin and pitted, no mirror
Not primer: it carries a metallic glint and pores
Avoid: big flat areas can read as unpainted primer in the sim, keep numbers light or they vanish.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 151 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 78 (satin gloss), clearcoat 59 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big flat areas can read as unpainted primer in the sim, keep numbers light or they vanish.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold orange, white or olive stripes: tactical contrast that stops it reading as primer; stencil lettering and markings: mil-spec look
Patterns to avoid: other speckle, grit or flake patterns: noise on noise; carbon or mesh: wrong mood
Spec overlays that work: matte dulling: more phosphate than metal; brushed spec: tool-steel direction
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Hardware: Rail Section
articles.summary: Charcoal anodised panel with a regular grid of slots, faint etched marks, satin sheen. Reads as a dark charcoal green-grey with a fine dotted screen effect; at a distance it is just a dull metal grey with slight shimmer.
articles.what: Slots at a fixed pitch, anodised, with the numbers laser-etched. Up close: Dark charcoal with a very regular grid of soft pale grey dots, about 5 px apart, like a perforated or knurled plate; dots are blurred and slightly greenish-grey, with faint darker mottling and cloud patches between. No visible etched numbers at this scale. From a distance: Reads as a dark charcoal green-grey with a fine dotted screen effect; at a distance it is just a dull metal grey with slight shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 183, roughness 69, coat 71. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: trim, sides, under stripes.
Fits: gt / sports car, truck / off-road, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Hardware: Rail Section" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Trim, bumpers, hood and splitter: reads like machined hardware
Whole body for a stealth build, but keep graphics bold
Dark ground: white, orange or yellow numbers read; the dots break up thin numbers.
Bold orange, red or white stripes: tactical contrast
Pairs well with: black, orange, white, red.
pitfalls: Not carbon fibre: round dots on a square grid, no twill
Not chain link or mesh: dots, not wire
Avoid: grid fights small sponsor decals, don't run it under busy graphics.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 183 (true metallic), roughness 69 (satin gloss), clearcoat 71 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: grid fights small sponsor decals, don't run it under busy graphics.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold orange, red or white stripes: tactical contrast; stencil lettering and serial-number marks: laser-etched look
Patterns to avoid: other grid, mesh or dot patterns: moire with the 5 px dots; busy graphics: the grid fights them
Spec overlays that work: brushed spec: machined aluminium direction; matte dulling: anodised feel
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Camo: Rain Pattern
articles.summary: Near-black charcoal grey with faint vertical dashed stripes, very desaturated, semi-matte. Reads as dark grey pinstripe fabric with a light dusting; the stripes survive, the ticks become soft grain.
articles.what: Vertical dashes over a base, the Eastern Bloc answer to everything above. Up close: Charcoal-black ground with a fine woven look, crossed by evenly spaced light grey dashed lines running almost vertical (tilted slightly right), about 40 px apart. Between them lie scattered short grey tick-marks in random directions, like flecks of rain. From a distance: Reads as dark grey pinstripe fabric with a light dusting; the stripes survive, the ticks become soft grain. Measured spec (average): metal 4, roughness 170, coat 145. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Camo: Rain Pattern" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body sides and doors: vertical lines suit tall panels
Roof and hood: stripes run front-to-back or side-to-side as rotated
Large white or red numbers read; thin ones get chopped by the lines.
Wide red or white stripes: strong accent on dark grey
Pairs well with: black, silver, white, red.
pitfalls: Not camo blobs: it is a pinstripe with random ticks
Not bright pinstripe: lines are muted grey
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers over the dashes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 4 (non-metal paint), roughness 170 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 145 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers over the dashes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: wide red or white stripes: strong accent on dark grey; big outlined numbers: the stripes are narrow, so large numbers read
Patterns to avoid: other stripe or camo patterns: collide with the lines
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat strip: sharpens the stripe contrast; rough matte spec: stealth tactical feel
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Night: Red Lens
articles.summary: Muted plum-to-rust gradient with fine horizontal grain, high gloss; soft dusty purple with warm streaks. Reads as a dark brick-red or maroon with a fine horizontal hatch and a warm orange fizz; the squiggles blur to a gritty burgundy, a bit like old CRT static.
articles.what: The filter that preserves dark adaptation, over a map at 0300. Up close: Very fine horizontal scan-line banding in dark maroon, plum and brick red, overlaid with tiny contour-map squiggles and loops in orange and amber 2-6px across, plus a few bright yellow-orange specks. Like a thermal screen or a red-filtered topographic map, sharply busy but narrow in tone. From a distance: Reads as a dark brick-red or maroon with a fine horizontal hatch and a warm orange fizz; the squiggles blur to a gritty burgundy, a bit like old CRT static. Measured spec (average): metal 47, roughness 35, coat 23. Shine: high gloss. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Night: Red Lens" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: the hatch reads as a texture on flats
Whole body also works: tone stays dark
White or cream numbers with a black outline read well; red or orange numbers disappear into the fizz.
Black or dark stripes and number panels: calm areas to read
Pairs well with: cream, gold, dark brown, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a plain deep red: has hatch and squiggle detail you can see up close
Not carbon fibre: horizontal bands only with wobbly loops
Avoid: bright green accents, heavy flake finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 47 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 35 (high gloss), clearcoat 23 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: bright green accents, heavy flake finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: black or dark stripes and number panels: calm areas to read; large simple graphics in black or cream: contrast against the red hatch
Patterns to avoid: line, weave, carbon or scan-type patterns: moire with the horizontal bands; fine speckle or flake: noise stacked on noise
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear boost: already near max, little gain; sparkle spec: more amber flicker
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
